newsitem.title: UK: Pro-British Protestants blamed for N.Irish attacks.
newsitem.headline: Pro-British Protestants blamed for N.Irish attacks.

text.p: Northern Ireland's police chief blamed pro-British militants on Monday for two recent attacks on Catholics that fanned fears of a new cycle of sectarian warfare.

"I would think that is the work of Loyalist extremist groups," Ronnie Flanagan said, referring to booby-trapped car attacks in December against two leading Catholic republicans who oppose British rule over the province.

It was the first security force confirmation of what politicians across the sectarian divide had suspected and came just hours before the resumption of multi-party talks aimed at reviving stalled peace efforts.
One of the bombs exploded and injured a well-known Belfast republican. The other was defused after it was spotted under the car of the other intended victim.
No group has claimed responsibiltiy for the attacks, which appeared to breach a Loyalist truce in force since October 1994.
Protestant politicians say that the truce is still in place because the guerrillas' umbrella group, the Combined Loyalist Military Group, has not made any statement that it is over.
Flanagan, speaking on BBC radio, said that violence by Loyalists was "as reprehensible as is violence by republican terrorists."
"At the moment, every attack carried out by republican terrorists brings more prominent the risk of a full resumption of Loyalist violence," he added.
